div.div: Which hops carry TLS today, who issues their certificates, and whether the client verifies them. The hop state is written on every edge: TLS verified / TLS unverified / PLAINTEXT / planned. Telemetry and datasource hops are collapsed to one edge per pair of tiers; the full per-hop list is the §12.1 table in docs/secrets/cert-manager.md. local-stack is plaintext by design and is not drawn.

div.div:
Reading the hop state
TLS verified: the client checks the chain against a CA and checks the hostname. TLS unverified: the hop is encrypted, but the client does not check who answers (sslmode=require, or a driver default of prefer). Every database hop was read from pg_stat_ssl on Kind (2026-10-01): PgDog, Keycloak, PgBouncer and replication are TLS 1.3; Temporal and the OpenBao DB engine are plaintext. PLAINTEXT: nothing is encrypted on the hop. Operator-managed TLS (CNPG replication and the PgBouncer client cert, the OpenBao Raft cluster port, Envoy Gateway xDS, chart webhook Issuers) uses each operator's own CA, not homelab-ca. platform-db's backups take the same plaintext S3 path as product-db's. kubelet and kube-apiserver scrapes use TLS with insecureSkipVerify.

div.div:
Planned, not installed (RFC-0020, provisional)
S0 edge issuer decouple · S1 OpenBao listener TLS · S2 CNPG server cert from homelab-ca · S3 pooler TLS · S4 apps on sslmode=verify-full through a pooler · S5 per-hop client certs · S6 gRPC + Temporal mTLS. Added 2026-10-01: S7 intermediate CA · S8 Keycloak HTTPS · S9 platform-db clients · S10 Envoy BackendTLSPolicy · S11 RustFS TLS · S12 Valkey auth + TLS · S13 OCI registry TLS + cosign · S14 KMS over HTTPS (production).
